title: Datum, trend, and risk learnability
hypothesis: Legal whole-well evidence can predict expensive baseline wells better than chance, while signed datum/trend actuation is authorized only if cross-fitted corrections improve pooled RMSE and survive spatial stress.

oracle_targets: additive per-well datum correction to last-known TVT
log baseline well RMSE for risk ranking
legal_inputs: MD, X, Y, and Z over the supplied whole well
horizontal-well GR values and missingness over the supplied whole well
ANCC, ASTNU, ASTNL, EGFDU, EGFDL, and BUDA supplied surfaces
design.feature_policy: All predictive features are computable from test-time inputs. Hidden TVT is used only to construct oracle analysis targets and evaluate cross-fitted predictions.
probe_models: training-fold-only correlation screening to at most 48 legal features
fixed-size deterministic shallow multi-output regression forest
no_evidence_baselines: training-fold mean datum plus trend correction
design.harsher_split: five contiguous spatial X-midpoint blocks, held out one block at a time
design.separation_rule: Risk ranking and signed action are evaluated independently. A useful risk model does not authorize a correction gate.
controls: oracle algebra against E001 datum and datum-plus-trend floors
design.promotion: Authorize feature-based signed action only for at least 0.15 pooled RMSE gain, at least 0.05 gain over the best training-fold-mean action, wins on at least four repeated maps, bounded p90 and worst-5% tail changes, material datum sign accuracy at least 0.56, datum correlation at least 0.15, positive spatial-stress gain, and passing controls. Promote risk evidence separately only when risk Spearman is at least 0.20 and AUC at least 0.62 on at least four maps with positive spatial-stress Spearman.
